snapshot.what_it_does: Bharti Airtel is the world's second-largest telecom operator by customer base, serving nearly 666 million customers globally through an integrated digital network and a diversified portfolio of services. Its integrated portfolio brings together mobility, broadband, digital TV, and enterprise solutions including data centres, cloud, cyber-security and digital platforms.

segments.name: Mobile (India)
segments.note: Integrated mobile services with pan-India coverage (prepaid/postpaid, international roaming, 5G); revenue ₹1,129,954 Mn, up 12.7% Y-o-Y; EBITDA ₹680,346 Mn, up 17.5% Y-o-Y

segments.name: Homes (India)
segments.note: Broadband (fibre and FWA, up to 1 Gbps) and fixed-line voice in 1,635 cities; FWA in 3,300+ cities; revenue ₹77,747 Mn, up 31.7% Y-o-Y; EBITDA ₹38,952 Mn, up 32.1% Y-o-Y

snapshot.geographies: Presence in 17 countries (including Bangladesh and Sri Lanka through associate entities); #1 integrated communications service provider in India and #2 mobile operator in Africa; the Airtel Africa Foundation operates across 14 countries.
key_facts: 17 countries of presence; 2 Bn+ population covered
India network: 345,912 towers, 1,187,894 mobile broadband base stations, 532,388 route km of optical fibre
Distribution footprint of ~0.9 million outlets reaching 97%+ of India's population

promised_vs_delivered.verdict: Management delivered on every near-term checkable promise: cloud deals, elevated capex, dividend progression, B2B growth, ARPU gains and the Africa stake swap. The large data center targets (1 GW, 25% share, 56 edge sites) and Airtel Money listing remain untested, and Nxtra's AI efficiency targets were never revisited.

bull.point: Revenue reached 58,539.1 in Q1 FY27, up 18.4% YoY, with EBITDA margin 56.7% and operating margin 32.4%.
Execution score high: 24 FY26 cloud deals, dividend ₹24 vs ₹16, Africa stake above 79%, B2B up 12%, ARPU ₹264.
Homes is scaling fast: revenue ₹77,747 Mn up 31.7% YoY, EBITDA up 32.1%, FWA across 3,300+ cities.

bear.point: Profit is volatile despite growth: PAT fell 55.1% YoY in Q3 FY26 and 33.5% in Q4 FY26, while PBT slipped to 9,960.3.
Capex nearly doubled to ₹13,390 Cr in Q1 FY27 from ₹7,200 Cr; free-cash-flow impact is not stated.
bear.cite: Q3 FY26 p.3; Q1 FY27 p.3

bear.point: Big optionality remains unproven: 1 GW, 25% data-center share, 56 edge sites and Airtel Money listing lack later progress; Nxtra AI metrics unrevisited.

watch: Q2 FY27 revenue/PAT: whether 15-28% revenue growth converts to positive PAT after two negative-YoY quarters.
Capex versus cash generation as home-pass/5G FWA rollout stays elevated; FCF not stated.
Concrete Nxtra/edge data-center, Google cloud and Airtel Money listing milestones versus stated timelines.
